flawed_step: The universal claim itself (Tutte's 1971 conjecture) is false.
counterexample: The Horton graph (96 vertices) is finite, simple, cubic, bipartite and 3-connected, and it has no Hamiltonian cycle (Horton 1976; Bondy–Murty). Smaller ones: the Ellingham–Horton graphs (54 and 78 vertices, 1983) and Georges' graph (50 vertices, 1989). How it works: bipartite gadgets have 3 outgoing edges, all attached to vertices of the same colour. Any Hamiltonian cycle uses exactly 2 of each gadget's 3 edges, and Horton's gadget forces one particular edge to be used. The gadgets are joined so these forced edges cannot all be used together, so no Hamiltonian cycle exists. The full edge list was not written out or checked by hand.
assessment_summary: The statement is Tutte's conjecture, disproved by Horton's 96-vertex graph. Smaller 3-connected cubic bipartite non-Hamiltonian graphs are also known (Ellingham–Horton, 54 vertices; Georges, 50 vertices). The verdict relies on these published results; the edge-by-edge check was not reproduced by hand.
